observations: DOC-12 (feature-map.md) explicitly splits the doc set's own feature list into 2 groups: 'Offer types' (Multibuy, Wholesale Pricing, Quantity Break — can stack/conflict with each other at cart level, which is the file's whole reason to exist) and 'Other features' (Variant Swatches, Translate Offers, Translate Portal, Analytics, Onboarding Dashboard, Ask for Review, AI Offer Creation — explicitly annotated 'unlikely to conflict with offer types'). This is a structural fact from the doc set itself, not my invention.

DOC-11 (decision-log.md) 2026-08-27 entry explicitly merged 3 help-center articles (Buy X Get Y, Quantity Breaks for Same Product, Volume Discounts for Subscription) into ONE feature 'Quantity Break' with 3 internal template variants, specifically to avoid documenting shared business rules 3 times. This is direct precedent against re-splitting those 3 templates into 3 feature_candidates.

DOC-11 2026-09-14 entries show a merge-then-revert of Translate Offers / Translate Portal: briefly merged, then QA directly corrected that they are two genuinely separate features (different surface: storefront offer/widget content vs merchant-facing Portal UI chrome). Final state (what DOC-07 and DOC-10 currently say) is: 2 separate features. Treating them as 2 separate feature_candidates matches the doc set's own settled conclusion, not the earlier reverted merge.

DOC-15 (product-custom-css.md) + DOC-11 2026-08-27 'Moved Custom CSS from features/ to product/' entry: Custom CSS is explicitly NOT an offer type / NOT its own feature — it's a single shared advanced-settings field confirmed present in Multibuy, Wholesale Pricing, and Quantity Break. This is a textbook object-level cross-cutting fact (contract §5, 'object kb.json' tier), not a feature.

DOC-14 (known-issues.md) has one entry explicitly tagged across 3 feature slugs at once ('quantity-break, wholesale-pricing-offer, variant-swatches — ...') describing a shared storefront rendering bug that reproduces 'across offer types and even with zero app offer present' — another cross-cutting fact, reinforcing that offer-type-level coupling is real and documented, not assumed.

DOC-12 'Known interactions' table contains ≥1 explicit unresolved business question: when 2-3 offer types' triggers overlap on the same cart, exactly one offer's discount applies but which one wins is not understood (flips between live tests) — table literally says 'Need confirm PO/Dev'. This must survive into a NEEDS_CONFIRMATION/OPEN_ISSUE later, not be resolved or dropped.

config/products/qik-volume.json product_note and doc_set_note both flag DOC-16/17/18/19/20 (and most of DOC-13) as skeleton/TODO with ~0 extractable claims expected. Confirmed directly by reading all 5 files: product-glossary.md is a literal '_TODO_ / _TODO_' table row, product-overview.md is a 9-line skeleton, testing-environments.md/testing-regression-checklist.md/testing-test-data.md are each <15 lines of '_TODO_' placeholders (testing-environments.md has exactly one real fact: QVL_BASE_URL env var / QVL-Staging repo — automation tooling info, not product behavior). dev-references.md (DOC-13) is a 13-line link index with 1 literal '_TODO_' (Slack channel) and otherwise just project/repo identifiers.
assumptions: Treated the 3 stacking/conflicting offer types (Quantity Break, Multibuy – Mix & Match Combo, Wholesale Pricing Offer) as 3 FEATURES under one umbrella OBJECT 'discount-offers', rather than 3 separate objects or 3 features of a generic shared object. Grounded in DOC-12's explicit framing (feature-map.md exists *because* these 3 interact at cart level) plus DOC-14's cross-tagged bug and DOC-15's cross-offer shared setting — i.e. there is real, documented, cross-cutting coupling between exactly these 3, which is the bar for object-level grouping per contract §5 ('object kb.json: boundary-set xuyên nhiều sub-type, hạ tầng cross-cutting'). This is a structural judgment call on my part (the docs don't use the word 'object'), flagged here so normalizer/orchestrator can override if they read it differently.

Treated each of the 7 'Other features' (Onboarding Dashboard, AI Offer Creation, Variant Swatches, Translate Offers, Translate Portal, Analytics, Ask for Review) as its OWN standalone object (object_key == feature_key, 1 feature per object), rather than grouping them under one shared 'portal-platform' object. Reason: unlike the 3 offer types, the doc set contains NO documented cross-cutting fact tying these 7 together beyond 'all live somewhere in the Portal' — and 'same surface' is exactly the kind of technical-not-user-goal grouping the contract warns against (same failure mode as grouping by endpoint/table list). Forcing them into one artificial object would manufacture a cross-cutting layer that isn't evidenced anywhere in DOC-01..DOC-20.

Did NOT create a feature_candidate for Custom CSS (DOC-15) — folded it into discount-offers' object-level cited_sections instead, per the decision-log precedent that explicitly moved it out of features/. DOC-15 is still assigned a discovery unit (doc-ingest-explorer must still process it; its content, thin as it is, becomes object-level kb for discount-offers, not a feature profile).

Did NOT create object/feature candidates from DOC-13, DOC-16, DOC-17, DOC-18, DOC-19, DOC-20 — all confirmed near-empty skeletons on direct read. Each still gets a discovery unit (doc-ingest-explorer must still touch every doc_source per Gate C0), but expected_artifact for these will mostly be not_documented entries, by design.

AI Offer Creation (DOC-02) is a generator *for* the 3 offer types but is itself a separate merchant tool with its own page/UI/usage-limit business rules (distinct from the offer types it generates configs for) — kept as its own object rather than folded into discount-offers, consistent with DOC-12 listing it in the 'Other features' group, not the 'Offer types' group.
unknowns: Object-level role is deliberately left null at the doc-set level (bootstrap-request.json.context.role, per its own note) — this doc set spans both merchant (Portal) and buyer/shopper (storefront) surfaces with no single declared role. Per contract C0-DOC this requires an object-level OQ (NEEDS_CONFIRMATION, role unspecified) for at least discount-offers, variant-swatches, and translate-offers (the 3 objects with real storefront/buyer-facing content) even though most individual claims inside them do carry a clear per-claim role. This is a downstream doc-ingest-explorer/normalizer responsibility, flagged here for visibility.

DOC-12's unresolved discount-priority business question (which of 2-3 overlapping offers' discounts wins) has NO identified deciding variable yet (flipped between the two live tests in feature-map.md) — must be preserved as an open business question, not resolved by inference, when discount-offers' claims are ingested.

DOC-15 (Custom CSS) itself flags via its own '_TODO_' that it's unconfirmed whether Custom CSS applies to any offer type beyond the 3 already confirmed (Multibuy, Wholesale, Quantity Break) — doc-ingest-explorer should not assume it's universal to all current/future offer types.

DOC-02 flags an unresolved overlap between this run's object boundary and a not-yet-shipped Jira epic (QVD-179 Sidekick app extension, status In Progress) that deep-links back into AI Offer Creation — left entirely out of scope here since it's explicitly 'not confirmed shipped' per the doc itself; future runs should re-check DOC-02 once QVD-179/QVD-176/QVD-177 ship.
